subtopics.title: Evaluate sin, cos, tan on calculator
subtopics.exposition: A calculator is used to determine the values of the trigonometric ratios for any angle. On a Casio calculator the opening bracket is automatically added after pressing sin, cos or tan, so after typing the angle you only need to press the closing bracket. To evaluate cos 48°, press cos, 48, ), = which gives 0.66913..., that is 0.67 correct to 2 decimal places. To evaluate 2 sin 35° (a coefficient times a ratio), press 2, sin, 35, ), = which gives 1.147152..., that is 1.15 correct to 2 decimal places. To evaluate tan^2 81° (a power), press (, tan, 81, ), ), x², = which gives 39.86345..., that is 39.86 correct to 2 decimal places. Alternatively, tan 81° can be calculated first by pressing tan, 81, ), =, and the stored answer then squared using the ANS and x² keys. To evaluate 3 sin^2 72°, press 3, (, sin, 72, ), ), x², = which gives 2.71352..., that is 2.71 correct to 2 decimal places. Alternatively, 3 sin^2 72° can be found by pressing sin, 72, ), =, then ANS, x², =, and then multiplying the stored answer by 3 using ANS, ×, 3. To evaluate (1/4) cos 27° (a fraction coefficient), press (, 1, ÷, 4, ), cos, 27, ), = which gives 0.22275..., that is 0.22 correct to 2 decimal places. Alternatively, (1/4) cos 27° can be found by pressing cos, 27, ), =, then ANS, ÷, 4, =. To evaluate (5/6) tan 34°, press (, 5, ÷, 6, ), tan, 34, ), = which gives 0.56209..., that is 0.56 correct to 2 decimal places. Alternatively, (5/6) tan 34° can be found by pressing tan, 34, =, then ANS, ×, 5, ÷, 6, =. sin squared theta means (sin theta) squared: sin^2 θ = (sin θ)^2. The squared notation sin^2 θ = (sin θ)^2 also applies to the other trigonometric ratios. The worked example shows the keys to press on a Casio calculator, and other calculators work in a similar way. Calculator answers are given correct to 2 decimal places, written after an approximately-equal sign with a decimal comma, for example 0.66913... ≈ 0.67.

subtopics.title: Evaluate reciprocal ratios
subtopics.exposition: When calculating with the reciprocal ratios, the reciprocal ratio must be converted to one of the standard trigonometric ratios sin, cos or tan. To evaluate sec 34°, first write sec in terms of cos, sec 34° = 1/cos 34°, since there is no sec button on the calculator. After writing sec 34° as 1/cos 34°, press 1, ÷, (, cos, 34, ), ), = which gives 1.206217..., that is 1.21 correct to 2 decimal places. To evaluate cot 49°, first write cot in terms of tan, cot 49° = 1/tan 49°, since there is no cot button on the calculator. After writing cot 49° as 1/tan 49°, press 1, ÷, (, tan, 49, ), ), = which gives 0.869286..., that is 0.87 correct to 2 decimal places.

subtopics.title: Test trigonometric statements
subtopics.exposition: To decide whether a statement is true or false for given angle values, calculate the left hand side of the equation on the calculator. With x = 25° and y = 65°, the left hand side sin^2 x + cos^2 (90° - y) is calculated by pressing (, sin, 25, ), ), x², +, (, cos, 90, -, 65, ), ), x², =, which gives 1. When the calculated left hand side equals the right hand side, the final answer is that the statement is true.

claims.claim: A calculator is used to determine the values of the trigonometric ratios for any angle.
Most scientific calculators are quite similar, but the calculator steps might differ depending on the calculator used.
The calculator must be in degrees mode.
sin squared theta means (sin theta) squared: sin^2 θ = (sin θ)^2.
The squared notation sin^2 θ = (sin θ)^2 also applies to the other trigonometric ratios.
The worked example shows the keys to press on a Casio calculator, and other calculators work in a similar way.

Alternatively, tan 81° can be calculated first by pressing tan, 81, ), =, and the stored answer then squared using the ANS and x² keys.

Alternatively, 3 sin^2 72° can be found by pressing sin, 72, ), =, then ANS, x², =, and then multiplying the stored answer by 3 using ANS, ×, 3.

When calculating with the reciprocal ratios, the reciprocal ratio must be converted to one of the standard trigonometric ratios sin, cos or tan.
Converting to sin, cos or tan is the only way to calculate the reciprocal ratios on a calculator.
